newsitem.title: CHINA: Aero International studies family of small jets.
newsitem.headline: Aero International studies family of small jets.

text.p: Aero International (Regional) has begun a study to produce a family of small-sized jets aimed at regional airlines, a top official of the aircraft maker said on Wednesday.
"We have started studies to create a dedicated family, a 50- and 70-seat aircraft," Patrick Gavin, chief executive officer of Aero International (Regional) (AIR), said at a press conference.
AIR is owned by French group Aerospatiale, British Aerospace Plc and Italy's Alenia, a unit of state-controlled Finmeccanica.
Growing regional travel, particularly in the United States and Europe, has drawn the company's attention to a need to create a family of 50- and 70-seat aircraft, Gavin said.
"Our intention is clear -- to be a leader of the regional market -- and we need to address all the needs of regional airlines," he said.
He added that the small-sized jets would make their entry into the market in 2001. Development costs are estimated at US$1 billion, he said.
While air travel in Asia is growing, Gavin said the region's demand for smaller sized jets would materialise later.
